name: Athletic Trainer
description: ⚠⚠⚠ A master's-entry, state-licensed clinical profession paying $62,520 — less than a licensed practical nurse earns on a certificate ($64,400), and less than every associate-degree clinical route on this site except paramedic. ⚠⚠ The profession moved to master's entry in 2022: CAATE states that after the fall 2022 term, baccalaureate degree programmes will no longer enrol students. ⚠ Florida's statute has not caught up and still reads as though a bachelor's is enough.
credentialNote: ⚠⚠⚠ A BACHELOR'S IN ATHLETIC TRAINING IS NO LONGER A ROUTE INTO THE PROFESSION. The Athletic Training Strategic Alliance decided in 2015 to move the professional degree to master's level, and CAATE states that after the fall 2022 term baccalaureate degree programmes will no longer enrol students — students entering the profession now enter a graduate programme. ⚠⚠ FLORIDA'S STATUTE STILL READS THE OLD WAY. Section 468.707, F.S. requires a bachelor's degree from a college or university professional athletic training degree programme accredited by CAATE, or a bachelor's plus completion of Board of Certification internship requirements, together with passing the BOC examination and holding current CPR and AED certification. ⚠ There is no loophole in that — a CAATE-accredited PROFESSIONAL programme is a master's now, so meeting the statute means holding one. But a student who reads the statute and stops there will draw the wrong conclusion, and the statute is the document most likely to be quoted at them. ⚠⚠ Florida still recorded 56 bachelor's degrees under this CIP in 2023, all at one institution — consistent with teach-out completions rather than an open route. ⚠⚠⚠ So ask any programme, in writing: which of your degrees is the CAATE-accredited professional programme, and will completing it make me eligible for the BOC examination? Anything less specific is not an answer.
bodyHtml:
⚠⚠⚠ The longest training on this side of the site, and one of the lowest medians

Athletic training is a master's-entry, state-licensed clinical profession. Here is what it pays against the routes it competes with for students:

RouteEntry credential2025 median
Dental hygienistassociate$98,100
Respiratory therapistassociate$82,280
Radiologic technologistassociate$80,110
Occupational therapy assistantassociate$72,300
Physical therapist assistantassociate$68,380
Surgical technologistassociate / certificate$64,650
Licensed practical nurse⚠ certificate⚠ $64,400
Medical laboratory technicianassociate$62,930
⚠⚠⚠ Athletic trainer⚠⚠ MASTER'S⚠⚠ $62,520
Paramedicassociate$60,600

⚠⚠⚠ A licensed practical nurse, on a certificate, out-earns an athletic trainer with a master's. Of the clinical health routes on this site, only paramedic pays less — and paramedic is an associate degree.

⚠⚠ This is not an argument against the profession. It is an argument for going in with the number in front of you, because almost nothing a prospective student reads puts it there. If the work is what you want, the pay is what it is; if you are choosing between rehabilitation careers on the numbers, look at the top of that table.

⚠⚠⚠ The degree moved in 2022, and Florida's statute did not

SourceWhat it says
✅ CAATE (the accreditor)⚠⚠ “After the fall 2022 term, baccalaureate degree programs will no longer enroll students.” Students entering the profession now enter a GRADUATE programme.
⚠ s. 468.707, F.S.requires “a bachelor's degree from a college or university professional athletic training degree program accredited by” CAATE, plus the BOC examination and current CPR and AED certification

⚠ There is no loophole. The statute requires a CAATE-accredited professional programme, and those are master's now, so satisfying it means holding a master's. But the statute is the document most likely to be quoted at a student, and read alone it says the opposite of the truth.

⚠⚠ The 2015 decision was taken by the Athletic Training Strategic Alliance, not by any legislature — so this is a profession that raised its own entry bar and is waiting for the statute books to notice.

⚠⚠ Florida's own data shows the migration happening

InstitutionCredentials (2023)
University of South Florida30 master's
Florida International University21 master's + 18 research doctorates
University of Central Florida18 master's
University of North Florida5 master's
University of West Florida2 master's
University of Florida⚠ 9 professional doctorates
⚠⚠ Florida State University⚠⚠ 56 bachelor's, and nothing else

⚠⚠⚠ 56 of Florida's 159 athletic training credentials were still bachelor's degrees in 2023, and all of them came from one institution. A 2023 graduate enrolled around 2019, so this is consistent with teach-out rather than with a route that is still open — but it is exactly the situation in which a prospective student can be shown a bachelor's and assume it leads somewhere.

⚠⚠ The course file shows the same migration mechanically. Florida carries 101 graduate ATR course numbers against 46 undergraduate, and of the 26 ATR courses carried by two or more public institutions, 22 are graduate. The undergraduate survivors are ATR2010C, ATR3102, ATR3132 and a special-topics shell. The professional curriculum has physically moved to the 5000 level.

The occupation

Athletic trainers (29-9091)
2025 median$62,520
Employed (2024)⚠ 33,900
Annual openings⚠ 2,400
Growth 2024–34✅ much faster than average (7% or higher)
Education54% master's, 37% bachelor's, 8% high school

⚠ Note the education row: 37% still report a bachelor's. That is the existing workforce, licensed under the old rule, and it will decline as the cohorts turn over. It does not describe the route open to you.

⚠⚠ And note the size. 33,900 people and 2,400 openings a year nationally — smaller than nuclear medicine plus sonography combined. Growth is strong in percentage terms on a small base.

⚠ What the work actually is

O*NET: conduct an initial assessment of an athlete's injury or illness to provide emergency or continued care; care for athletic injuries, using physical therapy equipment, techniques, or medication; evaluate athletes' readiness to play and provide participation clearances; collaborate with physicians to develop and implement comprehensive rehabilitation programs; apply protective or injury preventive devices.

⚠⚠ Read the third task. Evaluate athletes' readiness to play and provide participation clearances — that is a clinical decision made at speed, often with a coach, a parent and a crowd wanting a different answer. It is the hardest part of the job and it is why the profession raised its entry credential.

Necessary skills

  • Orthopaedic assessment under time pressure, on a field rather than in a clinic.
  • Emergency management — spine injury, cardiac arrest, exertional heat stroke — where your decision is the only one available for several minutes.
  • Holding a return-to-play decision against pressure. This is the professional core and it is mostly about character.
  • Rehabilitation programming and the patience to run it over months.
  • Working under physician collaboration while being the person actually present.
  • Tolerance for the schedule. Evenings, weekends, travel and seasons; it is not a nine-to-five profession and the pay does not compensate for that.

Advice

⚠⚠⚠ Confirm in writing which degree is the CAATE-accredited professional programme. Not “we have athletic training” — the exact programme, its accreditation status, and whether completing it makes you eligible for the BOC examination.

⚠⚠ Do not rely on s. 468.707. It says a bachelor's and it is behind the accreditor. Read CAATE, then the statute.

⚠ Look at the wage table before you commit to a master's. If rehabilitation is the interest rather than athletics specifically, the physical therapist assistant and occupational therapy assistant routes pay more on an associate degree, at three times as many institutions.

⚠⚠ If you do want this work, plan the exit as well as the entrance. Athletic training is hands-on patient care, so the hours count toward physician assistant admission, which needs about 3,200 of them and roughly doubles the median. A substantial number of athletic trainers use it as exactly that.

And take the undergraduate degree seriously as a separate decision. You need a bachelor's in something to enter a master's; make it one that leaves you somewhere if you change your mind — exercise science, biology or health sciences all do, and a bachelor's titled “athletic training” increasingly does not.

programs.note: The programme — 8 Florida public institutions, 159 credentials: 76 master's, 56 bachelor's all at Florida State, 18 research doctorates at FIU and 9 professional doctorates at UF. ⚠ Read its degrees note on why a bachelor's is no longer a route and why Florida's statute still says otherwise.

⚠⚠ The comparison to make before committing. A physical therapist assistant reaches $68,380 on an ASSOCIATE degree — above the athletic trainer's $62,520 on a master's — and Florida teaches it at 24 institutions against 8. ⚠ Different settings and different patients, but if rehabilitation rather than sport is the draw, look here first.

⚠ The same shape again: occupational therapy assistant at $72,300 on an associate degree. ⚠⚠ Named because these three programmes compete for the same students and their credential-to-pay ratios are strikingly different.

⚠⚠ A real onward route, not a neighbour. Athletic training is hands-on patient care, and PA admission turns on roughly 3,200 hours of it — so an experienced athletic trainer is a strong applicant for a profession paying roughly double. ⚠ Six Florida public programmes.

⚠ Named because on-field emergency management is EMS work and many athletic trainers hold both credentials. ⚠⚠ At 39 Florida institutions and about a semester for EMT, it is also the cheapest way to find out whether emergency decision-making suits you before committing to a master's.

⚠ Not a route in, but a common direction out: concussion policy, heat illness prevention and injury surveillance are population health, and athletic trainers move into that work. ⚠⚠ Florida teaches it at 8 universities.

courses.reason: Care and Prevention of Physical Injuries — 2 institutions (UF and USF). ⚠ Lower division, and one of only four undergraduate ATR numbers with more than one carrier. A good, cheap look at the subject before committing to a graduate programme.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Do not read undergraduate ATR coursework as progress toward certification. CAATE professional programmes are graduate, and Florida carries 101 graduate ATR numbers against 46 undergraduate.

courses.reason: Principles of Athletic Training — 2 institutions (Florida State and UCF). Pre-professional survey of the field.

Kinesiology and Pathomechanics — 3 institutions (Florida State, USF, UWF), the most widely carried undergraduate ATR course. ⚠ Its real value is as a biomechanics requirement for graduate admission rather than as professional preparation.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Written for athletic training majors at institutions whose professional programme has since moved to master's level — check what your institution now counts it toward.

courses.reason: Anatomy and Physiology I — 20 institutions. The universal prerequisite for every graduate athletic training programme, and the grade they look at.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Two equivalent packagings: BSC2085 plus BSC2085L at 20 institutions, combined BSC2085C at 7.

courses.reason: Anatomy and Physiology I Laboratory — 19 institutions. Usually required as a separate line.
Anatomy and Physiology II — 19 institutions. Cardiovascular and neuromuscular systems, which is most of what the assessment courses build on.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Also carried as the combined BSC2086C at 7 institutions.

courses.reason: Anatomy and Physiology II Laboratory — 19 institutions.
Physics I, algebra-based — 19 institutions. Required by many graduate programmes, and biomechanics assumes it.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Calculus-based PHY2048 is carried at 25; either usually satisfies the requirement, but check.

courses.reason: General Chemistry I — 15 institutions. A common graduate prerequisite, and the foundation for exercise physiology and pharmacology content.
Elementary Statistics — 39 institutions. Required for graduate admission, and evidence-based practice is a substantial part of the master's curriculum.
Introduction to Psychology — 33 institutions. Standard prerequisite, and the psychological side of injury and return to play is a real part of the job.
Human Nutrition — 13 institutions. A frequent prerequisite, and directly applied: hydration, energy availability and eating disorders are athletic training problems.
Exercise Physiology — 3 institutions. The core science of the field; where it is not available, most programmes accept an equivalent from the exercise science or kinesiology prefix.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Florida numbers exercise physiology under APK, PET and HSC at different institutions. Check which prefix your target programme names.

courses.reason: English Composition I — 39 institutions. Universally required, and clinical documentation is a licensed professional's legal record.
